about: The graduale of the formulary “Second Sunday after Epiphany” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: The Lord sent His word and healed them, and rescued them from their ruin. Let His mercies and His wonderful works for mankind give glory to the Lord.

a.g: Let His mercies and His wonderful works for mankind give glory to the Lord

ex.w014: Misericordiae and mirabilia are plural subjects: the mercies and wonderful works are pictured as giving praise. Confiteantur is a subjunctive expressing a call to praise. The second half shares that verb. Domino names the Lord as the recipient of praise. Filiis hominum can be read as a dative of benefit: the wonderful works are for mankind. Both halves direct praise to the Lord, not to people.
